key_insight: OT-ICA replaces proxy non-Gaussianity objectives in linear ICA with squared Wasserstein distance to a Gaussian, and proves this is maximized when a projection recovers an independent source.
engineering_relevance: This gives a gradient-based ICA method that can work without strong distributional assumptions, useful for signal separation, artifact removal, and source discovery in applied systems.
method: Measure non-Gaussianity with $W_2^2$ to a standard Gaussian instead of negentropy proxies.
Optimize a linear projection by gradient ascent so its output is maximally far from Gaussian.
Use the resulting projection as the recovered independent component in ICA.
evidence_signal: On simulated mixtures, OT-ICA outperformed proxy-based ICA methods across different latent distributions, and it also worked on EEG artifact removal and econometric price discovery.
watch_item: Performance depends on successful gradient optimization of the Wasserstein objective, so initialization and optimization stability may matter in practice.
paper_title: Linear Independent Component Analysis via Optimal Transport
